competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: U.S. yields are little changed into the Fed after a sharp midweek safety bid that took the 10-year back to 5 percent. Official SOFR is 3.90 percent, but the futures strip still prices a higher path through 2027. Oil is down more than 2 percent on the session, yet WTI and Brent remain elevated near 103 and 117 as Hormuz disruption and thin spare capacity stay in the tape. Equities are firmer on the crude slide; gold holds near 4,008 and VIX is around 19. The dollar is mixed: the euro is soft on French debt, the yen firmer on AI risk-off, and USDCAD sits near 1.40 with a Bank of Canada hike poll for 28 October. Japan core CPI printed 2.1 percent, keeping normalization live. Watch the Fed, Canadian hike risk, and whether oil's drop is demand destruction or just a pause in the Hormuz shock.

perma-bull.thesis: Mar-27 STIRs still print above cash (CORRA 3.005 vs 2.25, SOFR 4.41 vs 3.90, AONIA 4.845 vs 4.60), so the priced hike path has not been retraced. Firmer equities with oil down more than 2% is risk-on, not a growth break, and WTI still at 103 keeps the energy impulse alive into Fed/BoC week. Flattening the pay on a one-day Iran/oil headline would treat a non-retrace as a dovish reset. Stay short CORRA_2027-03 as the lead higher-for-longer growth expression; hold the SOFR and AONIA pays with it.
perma-bull.invalidation: Mar-27 implieds retrace toward cash (CORRA toward 2.25, SOFR toward 3.90, AONIA toward 4.60); or WTI and equities sell together, marking a demand scare rather than a supply headline; or Fed/BoC deliver an easing path that collapses the cash-to-implied hike gap. Triggers not present in the tape stay null.

dollar-king.thesis: The leftover dollar-Canada long is a paid rate-gap trade that has already given back rather than recaptured its high. The United States still pays 3.90 versus Canada's 2.25, and the ten-year sits near 5.00 after a midweek bid, but three-digit crude and a Canadian hike into 2.50 this week are now the binding other leg. I would not start a dollar-Canada long from a flat book at 1.3995 with WTI at 103.27, so this residual is harvested rather than warehoused. Any later dollar view versus Canada has to be a new, smaller initiation after the Canadian meeting, not leftover size hoping the old peak returns.
dollar-king.invalidation: The harvest is wrong only if crude loses three-digit status and Canada does not deliver the polled hike, restoring the policy-rate gap as the dominant dollar-Canada driver; that would justify a fresh smaller long, not a reinstatement of this residual. A Fed event this week alone is not enough to keep leftover size while oil stays three-digit into a Canadian meeting. Stop, target, and re-entry prints are null.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: Expected the leftover rate premium to stabilize or lift dollar-Canada; instead profits were given back as oil stayed three-digit and Canada priced a hike.
performance_reflections.lesson: The first cut from 8 million to 3 million was not a completed harvest. When three-digit oil and a rising Canadian hike impulse arrive after a paid dollar-Canada win, flatten if you would not initiate from zero; leftover reduced size still waits on peak recapture.

causal.original_belief: United States policy-rate premium versus Canada would keep dollar-Canada supported, so a residual long after the first cut would still earn the gap and could recapture the high.
causal.observed_reality: Crude stayed three-digit even after a more-than-2% session drop, Canadian hike impulse rose into the 28 Oct meeting, and the residual gave back profits instead of recapturing the peak.
causal.assumptions_right: The United States still pays more than Canada (3.90 versus 2.25, ten-year near 5.00). Dollar-Canada, not a cross, was the right expression of that gap.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Three-digit oil as a Canadian terms-of-trade and currency impulse; Canada's willingness to hike toward 2.50; the idea that leftover size after a paid win is a free option on peak recapture.
causal.causal_divergence: The rate gap remained, but oil and the Canadian hiking impulse became the binding near-term drivers, so the residual behaved like a short-oil and short-Canada-policy hold rather than a pure rate-differential position.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With oil already three-digit and a Canadian hike in the poll, the first harvest should have gone to flat, not to a still-large 3 million leftover that required a second review after giveback.
causal.future_implication: After a material dollar-Canada win, three-digit oil plus a rising Canadian impulse is a harvest to flat when you would not initiate from zero. Reduced leftover size is still a peak-recapture hold.

carry-is-king.thesis: March 2027 Canadian and Australian overnight-index forwards still sit well above cash, so the existing receives are paid to wait if policy undershoots those implied paths. Session weakness in crude weakens the inflation-backup story that would threaten those holdings; it is a reason to stay patient, not to exit.
